GAIN: Graph Attention Interactive Network for Inductive semi supervised learning over large scale graphs.

we propose a novel Graph Attention Interaction Network architecture that uses multiple types of aggregation functions to capture the different features of neighboring nodes and integrate them through the aggregator level attentions.

we design a new graph neural network model, GAIN, that uses multiple aggregators to gather different types of information from the neighboring nodes and integrates the outputs of the aggregators through the attention mechanism.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed GAIN model achieves state of the art inductive semi supervised learning over large scale graphs by integrating multiple types of aggregating information and explicitly modeling graph feature interactions.
our proposed model, GAIN, achieves state-of-the-art performance for node classification and link classification tasks.
our GAIN outperforms the current state of the arts on all the tasks, and the experiments show our model is robust to the size of graphs and the number of training samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our GAIN model is able to capture the different aspect of the neighboring information, and it can better learn the graph structure by using graph regularized loss and graph feature interaction mechanism.
our model is a novel GNN architecture that utilizes multiple types of aggregations and a graph regularized learning objective.
GAIN model can effectively learn from the graph structure information, and can capture the different aspects from the neighborhood information of the nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
using different types of aggregator and integrating them through an aggregator level attention mechanism is beneficial to the performance of GNN models.
using multiple types of aggregations and graph regularization can improve the performance of GNNs and the explicit feature interaction mechanism can further improve the performance of the GNNs.
by utilizing multiple types of aggregations and graph structure information, the expressive capability of the model is greatly increased and the performance is improved.
